CAP.title: Community-acquired pneumonia (lung infection caught outside hospital)

items: Pneumonia is an infection of the lung tissue. Community-acquired means you caught it outside hospital.
Most people with mild pneumonia can be treated at home, but your doctor will check how severe it is.
Cough, often productive (bringing up mucus), and fever.
Pleuritic pain (sharp pain when breathing in) and fast breathing.
Chest X-ray to confirm a new shadow on the lung.
Blood tests such as a blood count and CRP.
Pulse oximetry to check your oxygen level.
Your doctor will decide if you can be treated at home or need admission, using a severity score.
Antibiotics are chosen by your doctor.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Rest, drink fluids, and keep your appointments.
Ask your doctor how to take any medicine safely.
Your doctor may check your chest X-ray again after treatment, to confirm recovery.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Oxygen level below 92 percent on room air
Confusion, very fast breathing (30 or more a minute), or low blood pressure
